content.title: About
content.content: A ham sandwich on white bread is a classic sandwich consisting of two slices of soft white bread with sliced cooked ham between them, often complemented by mustard, mayonnaise, lettuce, and cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded ham sandwich dates back to the 19th century in the United States.
Ham used in the sandwich is typically pork, but turkey or chicken can be substituted.
White bread provides a soft texture that lets the flavor of the ham and condiments shine.
The sandwich is a staple in school cafeterias and quick‑service cafés.
In some regions it is served with pickles or sauerkraut for extra tang.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The sandwich provides quick energy from the carbohydrates in the bread and fats in the sauces.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: If cheese is added, the sandwich contributes calcium beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Fiber from lettuce
items.content: Leafy lettuce adds a modest amount of dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham is often salty, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Some hams contain nitrites, which can be harmful in large amounts.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: White bread contains gluten and is unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Mayonnaise and cheese can make the sandwich calorie‑rich; portion control is advised.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly stored ham can cause foodborne illness; keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The ham sandwich is usually eaten cold, cut in half. It can be dressed with mustard, mayo, lettuce, tomato, or cucumber. For a more filling version, add a slice of cheese and a few slices of avocado.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Keep sliced ham wrapped tightly and refrigerated at 0‑4 °C, using it within 3‑5 days.
